title: Automated exit criteria: multi-metric anomaly probes for model switches
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Goal: Implement an automated, low-noise exit/rollback triggering mechanism for model switches (canaries, A/B, and shadow experiments) that synthesizes multiple operational signals (latency, error rate, token cost, throughput) into a single decision pipeline. The system must prioritize avoiding false positives while ensuring rapid mitigation for real degradations.

Background: Current rollout guard logic relies on per-metric static thresholds which generate noisy rollbacks during transient load spikes. We need a multi-signal probe that:
- computes short-term anomalies relative to recent baselines,
- is cohort-aware (by customer tier / region / route),
- supports asymmetric sensitivity for customer-impacting metrics vs cost metrics, and
- exposes runtime knobs for SREs/PMs (grace windows, cooldowns, required signal quorum).

Proposed approach:
1) Signal ingestion: P95 latency, P99 latency, 5xx error rate, token cost per 1k tokens, requests/sec (throughput). Signals normalized to a rolling baseline (15m/1h) and converted to z-scores.
2) Per-cohort aggregation: Group traffic into cohorts (route, region, billing tier). Baselines computed per-cohort to avoid noisy global baselines.
3) Anomaly scoring: Use a weighted sum of clipped z-scores with metric-specific weights (default weights: latency 0.4, errors 0.35, throughput 0.15, cost 0.1). Weight set and sensitivity are configurable per rollout.
4) Changepoint filter: Apply a Bayesian online changepoint detector to suppress transient spikes. Only anomalies sustained beyond a short duration (default 60s) increase the alarm score.
5) Quorum + hysteresis: Require at least two distinct signals (e.g., latency + errors) above per-metric thresholds OR a single high-severity signal (e.g., >6 sigma error surge) to trigger escalation. When alarm score crosses critical threshold, enter "mitigation" state (see Mitigations).
6) Safety windows: Implement pre-commit observation window (canary window), mandatory cooldowns between escalations, and progressive traffic evacuation (10% -> 50% -> 100%) rather than abrupt full rollback.
7) Explainability: Emit human-readable rationale for each decision (metrics, cohorts, duration, and score) to the Console and to the rollout event log for postmortems.

Mitigations (ordered):
- Step 0: Raise alert to on-call + attach diagnostic snapshot (top routes, sample requests, recently deployed model hash).
- Step 1: Divert new requests for the affected cohort to shadow or baseline model, continue collecting samples for 2 minutes.
- Step 2: If anomalies persist, throttle canary traffic and start progressive rollback (10% decrements every 30s with re-validation).
- Step 3: If severe errors (5xx surge) detected, immediate full evacuation to baseline model and page SRE.

Acceptance criteria:
- The probe must be plumbed into existing rollout controller and visible in Console rollout timeline.
- Default sensitivity should yield <5% false-positive rollback rate on historical 30-day production trace replay (see Simulation results).
- Time-to-evacuate after confirmed severe regression should be <90s in nan+high-load scenarios.
- Decision rationale for every triggered mitigation must be available in rollout event logs.

Simulation results (progress):
- Ran 20 replay tests using last 45 days of traffic (subset: search-route, alpha-tier). Using default weights and a 60s sustain window we observed: precision 0.92, recall 0.88 for labeled regressions (labeling based on known incidents).
- False positives reduced from ~12% (legacy static thresholds) to ~3.8% under varied load patterns.
- Median time-to-detect sustained latency regression: 48s (P95).

Open trade-offs and decisions: 
- Weighting scheme: Default weights above are conservative towards latency and correctness; PMs requested more focus on token-cost when rollouts target smaller cost-saving variants. We'll add per-rollout weight overrides for PM use.
- Baseline window: 15m windows adapt quickly but can be noisy during diurnal shifts. We propose a hierarchical baseline (15m short + 6h long) and blending coefficients tunable per rollout.
- Changepoint vs rolling average: Changepoint detector reduces false positives at expense of slightly higher detection latency. We prefer it for customer-facing rollouts but will provide a low-latency mode for performance-critical internal experiments.

Implementation plan:
- Week 1: Signal ingestion plumbing + per-cohort baseline store (Diego, Priya).
- Week 2: Scoring engine, changepoint filter, and Console event wiring (Diego, Omar).
- Week 3: Integrate with rollout controller, mitigation primitives, and progressive rollback flow (Diego, SRE pairing with Mina).
- Week 4: Simulation runs, false-positive tuning, and runbook updates (QA + SRE + PM signoff).

Links & artifacts: 
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Anomaly+Probe+Design
- Simulation Dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollout-probe/simulations
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/3321
- Runbook draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-rollout-probe-runbook

Security & compliance notes: The system will attach sample request payloads only when sampling is enabled and scrub PII per current scrubbing pipeline. No long-term storage of raw samples.

Next steps (short-term):
- Resolve PM question on default weights for cost-focused rollouts (action: PM Blake to provide product guidance by 2026-03-14).
- Add observability hooks for token-cost per-model variant.
- Schedule SRE tabletop for teardown scenarios on 2026-03-16.
